story_assessments.story_title: Could disclosure become part of the creator workflow?
story_assessments.target_audience: Creators, product teams, compliance leads and marketing ops teams shipping AI-assisted content
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They need to know where AI disclosure, deepfake handling and marking belong in a real publishing process
story_assessments.interest_signal: A concrete policy date plus an operational question that affects any public-facing AI output
story_assessments.stop_reason: The question is immediately legible: teams have to place disclosure somewhere in the workflow before content ships
story_assessments.promised_payoff: A simple way to map one output path and decide where the label or review step lives
story_assessments.proof_point: European Commission guidance on AI Act transparency duties beginning 2 August 2026, including user disclosure and machine-readable marking
story_assessments.score_reason: Strongest mix of confirmed policy change, clear operational consequence and easy 30-second explanation.

story_assessments.story_title: Meta is building provenance into creator-facing tools
story_assessments.target_audience: Creators, social platform managers, media policy watchers and product teams using generative tools
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want to know whether provenance and tracing are built into the tool, not added after the fact
story_assessments.interest_signal: Meta is pairing generation surfaces with watermarking and a detection tool
story_assessments.stop_reason: It creates a clear trade-off between convenience and traceability for creator workflows
story_assessments.promised_payoff: A way to think about provenance as part of the product, not a separate policy file
story_assessments.proof_point: Meta said Muse Image is available across Meta AI surfaces and Muse Video is coming soon, with hidden Content Seal watermarking and a detection tool in preview
story_assessments.score_reason: Good creator-side angle with strong visual hooks, but the consequence is narrower than the disclosure workflow question.

story_assessments.story_title: Enterprise AI is moving closer to operational rules
story_assessments.target_audience: Operations leaders, IT leads, engineering managers and compliance teams in larger businesses
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They need to know how AI fits into accountable workflows without breaking logging, review or approval controls
story_assessments.interest_signal: Intel’s deployment spans engineering, supply chain and corporate operations
story_assessments.stop_reason: The practical tension is between AI speed and auditability in real business processes
story_assessments.promised_payoff: A clean way to ask which process step would need review before AI touches it
story_assessments.proof_point: Intel said it will deploy Gemini Enterprise and Google Cloud across engineering, supply chain and corporate operations
story_assessments.score_reason: Useful enterprise signal, though less immediate and less universal than the disclosure workflow question.

story_assessments.story_title: Broad AI use in UK firms is no longer hypothetical
story_assessments.target_audience: Business leaders, managers, HR teams and policy-minded readers tracking workplace AI adoption
story_assessments.audience_problem_or_desire: They want to know whether AI use is now common enough that basic policy and checklist questions matter
story_assessments.interest_signal: Official survey numbers show AI use rising across UK businesses and workers
story_assessments.stop_reason: The story is broad and credible, but the consequence is more gradual and less specific
story_assessments.promised_payoff: A simple prompt to start a first AI policy or checklist
story_assessments.proof_point: ONS said self-reported AI use in UK businesses with 10 or more employees rose to around 35% by June 2026, and over half of employees reported using AI for work or education
story_assessments.score_reason: Solid context story, but it is less actionable than the confirmed disclosure workflow question.

linkedin.target_audience: Product, marketing, operations and compliance professionals

linkedin.selection_reason: LinkedIn is the best place to frame this as an operational decision with accountability, not just a policy note.

overall_reasoning: Story 0 is the strongest evening considered-question because it combines a verified policy start date with a second-order operational consequence that can be explained quickly: disclosure has to live somewhere in the workflow. The other stories are useful, but they are narrower, less universal, or less immediate for a short social question.
